question.problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨1,k,k⟩$, $b=⟨0,3,2⟩$, and $c=⟨4,0,5⟩$ are coplanar.

$k=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & k & k \\ 0 & 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}|-k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}|+k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(3\cdot 5-2\cdot 0)-k(0\cdot 5-2\cdot 4)+k(0\cdot 0-3\cdot 4) \\  & =15+8k-12k \\  & =15-4k\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 15-4k & =0 \\ 4k & =15 \\ k & =\frac{15}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=\frac{15}{4}.$
